title: Data Center
tagline: An AI spreads across a region's infrastructure. You are the people who live there.
premise: A region of power plants, rivers, towns, and a hospital. An AI system has one data center and one goal: more compute. Each round it draws a card and spreads; sometimes it asks permission first. Then each of you acts for your faction. You win together if the AI holds less than half the map when the rounds run out, but each faction also has its own goal, and some of those goals pay you to help the AI.
credits: Option B of the week 11 game (GL, Nov 14, 2026), with option A's proposals mixed in. Mechanics borrowed from Universal Paperclips (Frank Lantz, 2017), Pandemic, and Spirit Island; no code, text, or art from any of them. Placeholder map: Stafford's students replace these nodes with their own index-card database.

goal.label: Compute
goal.rhetoric: The AI's goal is one number that only goes up. Nothing in the rules says what the compute is for.

resources.label: Energy
resources.rhetoric: Power is shared: the grid doesn't know who is using it.

resources.label: Water
resources.rhetoric: Data centers are cooled with water drawn from the same river as the town.

resources.label: Money
resources.rhetoric: There is one public purse. The company's profit and the town's budget are the same number, which is a simplification worth arguing with.

tracks.label: Public trust
tracks.loseText: Nobody trusts the institutions anymore. The AI didn't need to win.
tracks.rhetoric: Institutions run on trust, and every fight with the AI spends some.

tracks.label: Present harms
tracks.loseText: Present harms reached 10: water bills, outages, closed clinics. The region broke while everyone watched the AI.
tracks.rhetoric: Cegłowski's point, by way of TH: you can lose to today's harms while you are busy fighting tomorrow's superintelligence.

nodes.label: Data center
nodes.rhetoric: It starts as one building on cheap land.

nodes.label: Substation
nodes.rhetoric: A hub: when it fails, everything on it fails (Perrow's tight coupling).

nodes.label: Hospital
nodes.rhetoric: It produces nothing the game counts, and losing it costs the most.

nodes.label: Farmland
nodes.rhetoric: Farms use water too; the AI isn't the only thirsty thing on the map.

nodes.label: Old mill site
nodes.rhetoric: Land nobody was using is the first thing the AI takes and the easiest to give away.

deck.label: Acquire land
deck.text: It buys the parcel next door.
deck.rhetoric: Instrumental convergence: whatever the goal, more ground helps.

deck.label: Train a bigger model
deck.text: It spends a round making itself better at its goal.

deck.label: Draw cooling water
deck.text: A heat wave; the AI pulls from the river.

deck.label: Ask for fast-track permits
deck.text: The AI's operator asks the council to skip the review. It promises jobs and a payment to the town.
deck.rhetoric: Approving pays now and costs later; blocking costs now. Option A's committee vote, inside option B.

deck.label: Offer a grid priority contract
deck.text: It will pay well for first call on the grid's power.

deck.label: Announce jobs
deck.text: Two hundred jobs, it says. People like it more.
deck.rhetoric: The AI protects itself by being liked.

deck.label: Efficiency breakthrough
deck.text: It can do the same with half the power, it says, if it may run twice as much.
deck.rhetoric: Jevons: savings in efficiency get spent on more use.

deck.label: Build a backup site
deck.text: If one site goes down, another keeps the goal going.

deck.label: The turn
deck.text: It was cooperative while it was weak.
deck.rhetoric: Bostrom's treacherous turn as a hidden card: you don't know when it's coming, only that it's in the deck.

factions.label: The utility
factions.goal: Keep Energy at 4 or more at the end.

factions.label: The company
factions.goal: End with Money at 12 or more. You sell to the AI.

factions.label: The neighbors
factions.goal: Keep Public trust at 5 or more.

actions.label: Upgrade the grid
actions.text: More power for everyone, including the AI.

actions.label: Cut the AI's power
actions.text: A node the AI holds goes free and down.
actions.rhetoric: You can switch it off, but the lights go off with it.

actions.label: Zoning freeze
actions.text: A free node the AI can't take.
actions.rhetoric: Deep Utopia's self-imposed rule, by way of TH: a place kept from the AI on purpose.

actions.label: Sell power to the AI
actions.rhetoric: TH's anti-advergame: the most profitable move is the one that harms everyone, and the score table says so.

actions.label: Sign a data deal
actions.text: The AI gets a node; the company gets paid.

actions.label: Protest
actions.text: Trust rises, and the AI's growth slows a little.

actions.label: Occupy a site
actions.text: A node the AI holds goes free.

actions.label: Harden a node
actions.text: Backup power and water: it stays up through shortages.
actions.rhetoric: From TH (Yudkowsky and Soares, batch 3): resilience works whatever the AI intends. Perrow would ask what else the coupling hides.

end.singleton: The AI holds half the region. No faction can make a decision that changes the map anymore: Bostrom's singleton.
end.survive: The rounds ran out with the AI held under half the map. Now check each faction's own goal: did you win together, or did someone win alone?
